## Audit

```
TOPICAL SENSITIVITY AUDIT (Phase 5)
==================================================
Status: HOLD
Reasoning: The post's central premise — that a 'new 2025 medical billing cap' is now law — is directly contradicted by public record. SB 30, the Texas tort reform bill the post appears to describe, failed to pass: the Texas Legislature adjourned its 2025 session without enacting it after the Senate and House could not reconcile their versions. Publishing a post telling injury victims their settlements will be 'shrunk' by a law that does not exist could mislead clients, expose the firm to Bar complaints for publishing inaccurate legal information, and severely damage credibility if readers fact-check. This is a factual accuracy hold, not a tone/tragedy hold.
Relevant recent events:
  - Texas SB 30 died June 2, 2025 — the Texas Legislature failed to agree on a final version before the end of the 89th legislative session; the bill never became law.
  - In its final form, SB 30 was stripped of all major tort reform provisions and covered only health care disclosures; neither SB 30 nor companion HB 4806 became law in 2025.
  - Texans for Lawsuit Reform has stated it will push the issue to the 90th Texas legislative session — meaning the 'new law' described in the post does not currently exist.
  - No recent Houston-area mass casualty events, major tragedies, or public mourning periods identified in the 7–14 day window that would independently trigger a tone/sensitivity hold.
Search queries used:
  - Texas tort reform medical billing 2025 news
  - Houston Texas mass casualty tragedy June 2026
  - Texas SB 30 tort reform signed into law 2025 status
```
